q: Where should a login token be saved on the phone?
options: In a secure store (SecureStore, Keychain or Keystore)
In AsyncStorage, because it is easy
In plain MMKV with no encryption key
In the app code, as a constant
why: The React Native security guide says Async Storage is unencrypted and lists token storage as a thing not to do with it. Keychain on iPhone and an encrypted store on Android are made for secrets.

q: Which statements about AsyncStorage and MMKV are true?
options: AsyncStorage calls are async, so you await them
MMKV calls are synchronous through JSI
why: AsyncStorage is asynchronous and unencrypted. MMKV is synchronous, and by default it keeps plain text. It encrypts only if you give it an encryption key.

q: In an outbox, you should remove an item from the saved queue before you send it, so it is not sent twice.
why: No. Send first and remove the item only after the server said ok. If you remove it first and the call fails, the data is lost.

q: Put the offline first steps in order.
items: The user acts and the app saves it on the phone
The app shows the result at once
Later, when online, the app sends the first item from the outbox
The server says ok and the app removes that item from the outbox
why: Save locally first, show it, send later, and remove an item only after the server confirms it.

q: The saved data says version 5, but the running code only knows version 3. What should a safe store do?
options: Return the fallback value and do not crash
Run the version 3 code on it anyway
why: Data from a newer version can have a shape the code does not understand. Use a default value. Migrations only move data forward, one step at a time.

q: To keep the order of 5,000 products searchable by price on the phone, you would use a ______ database. (one word)
why: SQLite can filter and sort inside the database with a query such as SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < 50, instead of loading everything into JavaScript.
